Independent native review by Grok 4.7, effort high, in this session. No delegated reviewer. Source at candidate `3fd82526c0baa2d975ed6eda50487b75c6e68d51` was the authority. Tests were not re-run.

## Findings

### 1. Major — `OnNameConflict::AddRevision` does not attach a revision once the sibling lock is held

Paths: `packages/drive/src/Operations/FileOperations.php` lines 46–55 and 122–151; `packages/drive/src/Actions/Files/IngestFileAction.php` lines 100–102; `packages/drive/src/Actions/Nodes/NameConflictResolver.php` lines 22–28.

`files()->upload(..., onConflict: AddRevision)` looks up the sibling with a case-sensitive `where('name', …)` before the transaction. Under the parent lock, ingest always calls `NameConflictResolver`, and that resolver throws `NodeNameConflictException` whenever `onConflict` is not `Rename`.

Sibling uniqueness is `lower(name)` (`NodeReadRepository::siblingNameExists`). Two concrete failures:

- An existing `Report.pdf` and an upload named `report.pdf` with `AddRevision` miss the pre-check, then fail with a name conflict. No revision is added, and Edit is never evaluated on that path.
- Two exact-name `AddRevision` uploads of a new name both miss the pre-check. The first creates the file. The second waits on the same parent lock, sees the sibling, and throws the same conflict instead of adding a revision.

The adopted contract requires the central resolver to treat `AddRevision` as upload-only, and to authorize Edit on the existing file before the revision write. `Fail` and `Rename` are implemented. UPGRADE and CHANGELOG describe the Edit check as current behavior.

Correction: under the locked sibling predicate, resolve `AddRevision` to the existing file, require Edit, then call the revision action. Keep the folder-sibling conflict. Re-qualify the upload name-conflict cases, including a case-variant and the locked same-name pair. A full package sweep is not required.

### 2. Major — kind-scoped list cursors accept a different kind filter

Path: `packages/drive/src/Queries/NodePageQuery.php` line 42, with `ListOptions::$kinds` as `list<NodeKind>` (`packages/core/src/Data/Drive/ListOptions.php` lines 13–19) and `enum NodeKind: string` (`packages/core/src/Enums/Drive/NodeKind.php` line 23).

The HMAC context is `json_encode([…, 'kinds' => $options->kinds, …])`. PHP encodes a backed enum as `{}`, so `[NodeKind::File]` and `[NodeKind::Folder]` produce the same signed context. `ExactListing::decode` then accepts the cursor.

A cursor minted for files in a folder is replayed as the folder listing. The keyset still advances from the file page’s last inspected `(position, name, id)`, so folders at or before that position are skipped. Drive, tenant, folder, sort, and direction remain bound. The kind component does not.

The adopted contract requires the signed cursor to include kind. `ListChildrenQuery`, `SearchQuery`, and `ListTrashQuery` all go through this identity.

Correction: put scalar kind values in the signed identity. Re-qualify one list test that a file cursor is rejected for a folder filter. Do not broaden into unrelated suites.

### 3. Major — shared-list cursors are not bound to the actor

Paths: `packages/drive/src/Queries/SharedWithActorQuery.php` line 27; `packages/drive/src/Http/Controllers/NodeController.php` lines 56–60.

The HMAC context is the constant `shared:*:`. The candidate query is correctly limited to `sharedNodeIds($actor)`, so another user does not receive the first user’s rows. The signature still validates for every caller. Replaying actor A’s cursor on actor B’s shared list starts B after A’s last `(name, id)` and skips B’s earlier shared nodes.

The adopted contract includes `SharedWithActor` in the signed scope cursor (drive, tenant, filter, kind, direction, folder/within as applicable). This listing has no per-actor filter in the signature.

Correction: bind the actor identity into the signed context. Re-qualify the shared listing cursor with two actors. A full drive sweep is not required.

### 4. Minor — Unreleased upgrade text still says the removed facade entry points remain

Path: `UPGRADE.md` line 507, in the Unreleased section “Drive names and handle methods (AD03, AD04)”.

That sentence says `Vaulter::for()` and `forStorage()` remain. The P3.3 section at lines 11–13 correctly says those calls are removed and maps them to `Vaulter::drive()`. Both statements are in the same Unreleased guide. `VaulterManager` and the `Vaulter` facade no longer expose the old methods.

Correction: make the older Unreleased sentence match the removal map. Doc check only.

## Checked without a demonstrated defect

The facade and `DriveHandle` match the canonical map: immutable `actingAs` / `asSystem` / `withCorrelationId`, lazy guard user, persisted drive key, and named `handle` extension. Old flat calls are gone from executable package code. `OperationGuard` returns 404 when View is missing and 403 when a later ability is missing. Filament rename, move, trash, restore, and purge go through that handle. `NodeLocator` uses the raw key and `drive_id`.

Sequence is a signed nonnegative BIGINT, rejected on 32-bit PHP, compared under the row lock, bumped once per changed aggregate, and left at 0 for new nodes. No-op rename and update do not bump. Copy does not bump the source. Installed document overwrite and append, and both Yjs branches, call the helper. Trash, purge, and file revision restore keep the Tree → sorted node → file → revision → quota → CAS order. Unsupported document and shortcut copies are rejected for the whole subtree before inserts. Destination `scan_status` comes from current admission. Infected sources are refused. Legacy `not_required` is used only when every spec is off. Purge deletes node rows in the same transaction. `empty()` and `vaulter:purge-trash` continue after a root failure, skip unauthorized or no-longer-eligible roots, and surface failure after the walk. Committed upload replay re-checks owner and ability, compares the stored payload hash and node, revision, and blob pointers, returns before a second ingest, and does not compare the old expectation to the live sequence. Cleanup is registered with `afterCommit`. File read uses the file-scoped revision and `BlobStore::read`. The download response closes the stream. Docs for defaults (`Fail` on upload, move, and folder create; `Rename` on copy and restore; suffixes `(2)`–`(6)`) match the resolver. P3.7 evidence and work, P3.8 strict tenant wiring, and P4 document aggregate operations are not claimed as done.

Executor receipts record preserved base failures and later green affected lanes, including NC-SEQ and NC-SEQ-BOUND restored to the same `NodeSequence.php` hash. This review did not re-execute those commands and does not treat a deferred P3.8 barrier as a missing P3.3 proof.
